name: Retro Cocktail Jewellery
summary: Big, curved jewels in warm yellow and rose gold, set with large coloured stones. The forms are bows, ribbons, flowers and bracelets of links. They were made in the years of war and wartime metal rules.

philosophy.core_thesis: A jewel is a bold, warm sculpture in gold: large, curved forms and bright coloured stones that gain from the dress and the cocktail hour.
design_principles: Use gold, yellow and rose, as the main metal; platinum is scarce in the war years.
Sculpt the metal into bows, ribbons, scrolls, flowers and folds that look like cloth.
Set large coloured stones, such as aquamarine, citrine, amethyst and topaz, in a simple frame.
Add small rubies, synthetic rubies or sapphires as a point of colour.
Make the piece big. A cocktail ring is 2 to 3 cm, a brooch is 6 to 9 cm and a bracelet is 2 to 4 cm wide.
Build a bracelet of curved links like a tank track, a gas pipe or a woven strap.
Make a clip brooch in pairs that can be worn as one piece on the lapel or the neckline.
Polish the gold bright, and set it in contrast to a few matte or woven areas.

silhouette.shape: A large, sculpted jewel in gold: a ribbon bow, a flower clip, a cocktail ring or a thick bracelet of links.
silhouette.line: Curved and rounded, with ribbons, scrolls and folds; the shape is thick and soft.
silhouette.fit: A clip sits on the lapel or the shoulder, a bracelet lies loose on the wrist, a ring sits high on the finger.
silhouette.proportion: A cocktail ring is 2 to 3 cm across. A clip is 6 to 9 cm wide. A link bracelet is 2 to 4 cm wide and 15 to 18 cm long.
rules: Wear a pair of clips at the neckline of a dark dress.
Set one large stone in a ring with a gold ribbon shank.
Link a bracelet in thick, curved gold in the style of a tank track.
Add a spray of small rubies to the centre of a gold bow.

fabrics.rule: Make the jewel from warm gold with large, bright coloured stones, and use diamonds only in small points.

methods: sculpted and chased gold in folds and ribbons
large stones in simple, closed bezels
thick curved links like a tank track
double clips that join into one brooch
construction.closures: A double pin clip on a brooch; a hidden box clasp with a safety chain on a bracelet; a clip back on an earring.
construction.details: A ribbon bow, a scroll, a flower, a large citrine or aquamarine, and a spray of small rubies.

surface.pattern: Folds, ribbons and scrolls in relief, with a large smooth stone at the centre.
surface.gloss: High on the polished gold, 80 to 95 GU, with a few brushed or woven areas for contrast.
surface.wear: Thick gold takes wear well and gets small dents; the style accepts a soft, used look.

palette.strategy: Warm yellow and rose gold with large, bright stones in one strong colour.

processes: polishing and brushing of the gold
making.scale: New York and Paris houses and a few independent studios; many pieces by hand, in small runs.
making.signs: Thick curved gold, a large central stone, a ribbon or a scroll form and a high polish.

pieces.form: Pair of gold bow clips with a spray of small rubies
Cocktail ring with a large citrine in a gold ribbon shank
Thick curved link bracelet in the tank-track style
Clip earrings in the form of a gold flower
Gold ribbon necklace with a bow and a drop

positive: double clip brooch at the neckline
large aquamarine in a gold frame

canonical_works.work: Gold and gem flower clip brooches

evidence.title: Van Cleef and Arpels jewellery advertisement, Vogue, 15 November 1943

emotion.target_response: A warm, confident and glamorous feeling: the viewer sees a rich, soft glow at an evening party.

use_cases: a gold jewellery line with a bold form
a museum label for a Retro piece
an image prompt for 1940s evening glamour
avoid_when: the brief wants a cold, white and geometric look
the brief wants quiet, small jewels

modifiers.how: Swap gold for platinum, straighten the curves, and add black onyx and baguette stones.
Remove the ribbons and the bows, rough up the gold, and set uncut stones.

ornament_level.note: Folds and ribbons give the ornament; a plain bracelet of links sits at the low end.
